_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-microbiology.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). Samples: FMGE recalls, no images.
subject: Microbiology
intro: Microbiology in FMGE is a game of pairs: organism and medium, organism and stain, test and disease, vaccine and type. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

mic.gen.media.note: Selective media: Thayer-Martin (Neisseria), TCBS (Vibrio, yellow colonies), Lowenstein-Jensen (TB), Löffler serum slope and potassium tellurite (diphtheria), MacConkey (lactose fermenters pink), XLD/DCA (Salmonella, Shigella), Bordet-Gengou (pertussis), Sabouraud (fungi). Chocolate agar: Haemophilus (needs factors X and V).
mic.gen.media.why: Modified Thayer-Martin medium has antibiotics that suppress normal flora, so Neisseria can be isolated.

mic.gen.stain.note: Gram stain: crystal violet, iodine, decolouriser, safranin. Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast): TB with 20% sulfuric acid, leprosy with 5%. Albert stain: metachromatic granules of diphtheria. India ink: Cryptococcus capsule. Giemsa: malaria and blood parasites. Gomori methenamine silver: Pneumocystis and fungi.
mic.gen.stain.why: Albert's stain shows the metachromatic (volutin) granules of Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

mic.gen.steril.note: Autoclave: 121 °C for 15 minutes at 15 psi (spore test: Geobacillus stearothermophilus). Hot air oven: 160 °C for 2 hours (glassware, powders, oils). Tyndallisation: steaming on 3 days for sugar and gelatin media. Ethylene oxide and plasma (hydrogen peroxide) for heat-sensitive equipment. Prions need special methods.
mic.gen.steril.why: Tyndallisation (intermittent steaming) sterilises media with sugars and gelatin that autoclaving would damage.

mic.gen.disinf.note: Blood spills: sodium hypochlorite (1% for spills). Glutaraldehyde 2%: endoscopes (high-level disinfection). Alcohol 70% works better than absolute alcohol. Chlorhexidine for skin. Spores are killed only by sterilants (glutaraldehyde with long contact, ethylene oxide, autoclaving).
mic.gen.disinf.why: Sodium hypochlorite inactivates blood-borne viruses and is the standard for blood spills.

mic.gen.genet.note: Transformation: naked DNA taken up. Transduction: DNA carried by a bacteriophage. Conjugation: DNA passed through a sex pilus (plasmids, drug resistance). Lysogenic conversion gives toxins: diphtheria, botulinum, cholera, Shiga-like, scarlet fever toxins.
mic.gen.genet.why: DNA moved from one bacterium to another by a bacteriophage is transduction.

mic.bac.cocci.note: Staph aureus: coagulase positive, golden colonies, catalase positive. Lancefield grouping uses the C carbohydrate of the cell wall. Group A strep: bacitracin sensitive, rheumatic fever and glomerulonephritis. Pneumococcus: optochin sensitive, bile soluble, lancet-shaped diplococci. Enterococcus grows in 6.5% salt and bile.
mic.bac.cocci.why: Lancefield groups are based on the C carbohydrate antigen in the streptococcal cell wall.

mic.bac.enteric.note: Typhoid: blood culture in week 1 (the best test), Widal from week 2, stool and urine cultures in weeks 3-4; the gallbladder holds carriers. Shigella: non-motile, the lowest infective dose. E. coli types: ETEC (traveller's diarrhoea), EHEC O157:H7 (HUS). Salmonella makes H2S.
mic.bac.enteric.why: Blood culture is most often positive in the first week of enteric fever.

mic.bac.vibrio.note: Comma-shaped, darting motility, TCBS agar gives yellow colonies (sucrose fermenter). Alkaline peptone water for enrichment. Cholera toxin raises cAMP: rice-water stools. O1 (El Tor) and O139 cause epidemics. Treat with ORS; doxycycline or azithromycin shortens it.
mic.bac.vibrio.why: Vibrio cholerae ferments sucrose and makes yellow colonies on TCBS agar.

mic.bac.tb.note: CBNAAT (Xpert MTB/RIF) detects TB and rifampicin resistance in about 2 hours. Line probe assay: rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in a day or two. LJ culture takes 6-8 weeks; liquid culture (MGIT) is faster. Cord factor makes serpentine cords; niacin test positive.
mic.bac.tb.why: Xpert MTB/RIF (CBNAAT) gives TB and rifampicin resistance in about 2 hours.

mic.bac.clost.note: C. botulinum: blocks acetylcholine release, descending flaccid paralysis (canned food, honey in infants). C. tetani: blocks inhibitory transmitters (GABA, glycine), spastic paralysis, drumstick spores. C. perfringens: gas gangrene, Nagler reaction, double zone of haemolysis. C. difficile: pseudomembranous colitis after antibiotics.
mic.bac.clost.why: Botulinum toxin stops acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, causing flaccid paralysis.

mic.bac.pseudo.note: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: oxidase positive, non-fermenter, blue-green pigment (pyocyanin), grape-like smell. Infects burns, cystic fibrosis lungs, ventilators, swimmer's ear. Treat with anti-pseudomonal drugs (piperacillin-tazobactam, ceftazidime, aminoglycosides).

mic.vir.hep.note: HBsAg: current infection. IgM anti-HBc: acute infection, and the only marker in the window period (HBsAg gone, anti-HBs not yet up). HBeAg: high infectivity. Anti-HBs alone: vaccinated. Hepatitis A and E spread faeco-orally; E is dangerous in pregnancy. Hepatitis D needs hepatitis B.
mic.vir.hep.why: In the window period HBsAg and anti-HBs are both negative and only IgM anti-HBc is positive.

mic.vir.hiv.note: HIV-1 subtype C is the commonest in India. gp120 binds CD4, with CCR5 or CXCR4 co-receptors. India's testing uses three different rapid tests (ELISA-based). Infants: DNA PCR, since maternal antibodies last up to 18 months. Viral load monitors treatment.
mic.vir.hiv.why: Subtype C causes most HIV-1 infections in India.

mic.vir.herpes.note: EBV: infectious mononucleosis (Paul-Bunnell heterophile test, atypical lymphocytes), Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal cancer. CMV: owl's eye inclusions, the commonest congenital infection. HSV: Tzanck smear (multinucleated giant cells), HSV-1 encephalitis in the temporal lobe. VZV: chickenpox and shingles. HHV-8: Kaposi sarcoma.
mic.vir.herpes.why: The Paul-Bunnell test detects heterophile antibodies in infectious mononucleosis.

mic.vir.torch.note: Congenital rubella: PDA, cataract, deafness. CMV: periventricular calcification, deafness. Toxoplasma: hydrocephalus, chorioretinitis, scattered brain calcification. Syphilis: Hutchinson teeth, saddle nose, snuffles. HSV: skin, eye and mouth lesions, encephalitis.
mic.vir.torch.why: Cataract is a feature of congenital rubella, not HSV.

mic.myc.candida.note: Candida albicans: germ tube test positive within 2 hours in serum, pseudohyphae, chlamydospores on cornmeal agar. Risk: diabetes, antibiotics, steroids, HIV. Candida auris: drug-resistant, spreads in hospitals.
mic.myc.candida.why: Candida albicans forms germ tubes in serum at 37 °C within 2 hours.

mic.myc.dimorph.note: Dimorphic fungi: mould in the cold, yeast in the body. Histoplasma (bird and bat droppings, inside macrophages), Blastomyces (broad-based budding), Coccidioides (spherules), Paracoccidioides (ship's wheel), Sporothrix (rose gardener's disease, cigar-shaped yeast, spreads along lymphatics), Talaromyces marneffei.
mic.myc.dimorph.why: Histoplasma capsulatum is a dimorphic fungus; Aspergillus, Candida and Rhizopus are not.

mic.myc.asp.note: Aspergillus: septate hyphae branching at acute angles (45°); fungus ball, ABPA in asthma, invasive disease in neutropenia; voriconazole. Mucor/Rhizopus: broad aseptate hyphae at right angles; rhino-orbito-cerebral disease in diabetic ketoacidosis; amphotericin B and surgery.
mic.myc.asp.why: Septate acute-angle hyphae in an asthmatic with worsening symptoms point to allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis.

mic.par.malaria.note: Falciparum: multiple delicate rings, appliqué (accolé) forms, banana-shaped gametocytes, Maurer dots. Vivax and ovale: Schüffner dots, enlarged red cells, hypnozoites (relapses; primaquine). Malariae: band forms, 72-hour fever. Thick smear to find, thin smear to identify species.
mic.par.malaria.why: Several fine rings in one red cell and appliqué forms are typical of P. falciparum.

mic.par.filaria.note: Wuchereria bancrofti, spread by Culex; microfilariae show nocturnal periodicity (take blood at night). The membrane filtration concentration method is the most sensitive for microfilariae. Immunochromatographic card test detects antigen by day. DEC with albendazole for mass treatment.
mic.par.filaria.why: Filtering a large blood volume through a membrane concentrates microfilariae, making it the most sensitive method.

mic.par.amoeba.note: Entamoeba histolytica: cysts with 4 nuclei, trophozoites with ingested red cells. Flask-shaped colonic ulcers; amoebic liver abscess (anchovy sauce pus, right lobe). Treat with metronidazole, then a luminal agent (diloxanide, paromomycin).
mic.par.amoeba.why: The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica has four nuclei.

mic.par.toxo.note: Cats are the definitive host; humans get it from cat faeces (oocysts) or undercooked meat (tissue cysts). Tachyzoites cross the placenta. Congenital triad: hydrocephalus, chorioretinitis, intracranial calcification. In HIV: ring-enhancing brain lesions.
mic.par.toxo.why: Tachyzoites, the rapidly dividing form, cross the placenta to the fetus.

mic.par.helm.note: Hookworm enters through the skin of bare feet; causes iron deficiency anaemia. Hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus, dogs): rupture can cause anaphylaxis. Taenia solium: neurocysticercosis (pork). Diphyllobothrium latum: B12 deficiency. Strongyloides: autoinfection, hyperinfection with steroids. Enterobius: perianal itch, Scotch tape test.
mic.par.helm.why: A hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus) that ruptures can cause anaphylactic shock.

mic.imm.vacc.note: Live attenuated: BCG, OPV, measles, MMR, rotavirus, varicella, yellow fever, oral typhoid. Killed/inactivated: IPV, rabies, hepatitis A. Subunit/recombinant: hepatitis B, HPV. Toxoids: tetanus, diphtheria. Conjugate: Hib, pneumococcal, meningococcal.
mic.imm.vacc.why: MMR is live attenuated; hepatitis B, rabies and IPV are not.

mic.imm.cold.note: Routine vaccines are stored at +2 to +8 °C. OPV is the most heat-sensitive and can be frozen (−15 to −25 °C). Freeze-sensitive: hepatitis B, DPT, Td, pentavalent, IPV, PCV, rotavirus (never freeze; shake test if in doubt).
mic.imm.cold.why: Most routine vaccines are kept at +2 to +8 °C.

mic.imm.hyper.note: Type I: IgE, mast cells (anaphylaxis, hydatid cyst rupture, asthma). Type II: antibodies against cells (transfusion reactions, Rh disease). Type III: immune complexes (serum sickness, Arthus, post-strep GN). Type IV: T cells, delayed (Mantoux, contact dermatitis, granulomas).

mic.imm.def.note: B cell: X-linked agammaglobulinaemia (Bruton, BTK), recurrent bacterial infections after 6 months. T cell: DiGeorge (22q11, no thymus, low calcium). Both: SCID (adenosine deaminase deficiency). Phagocyte: chronic granulomatous disease (NADPH oxidase, NBT test). Wiskott-Aldrich: eczema, low platelets, infections.
mic.imm.def.why: X-linked agammaglobulinaemia is a B-cell defect; DiGeorge is a T-cell defect.

mic.imm.agab.note: Epitope: the part of the antigen that binds; paratope: the part of the antibody that binds it. IgM appears first in a primary response and is the biggest (pentamer); IgG crosses the placenta; IgA is in secretions; IgE in allergy and worms. Precipitation, agglutination and complement fixation are classic reactions.
mic.imm.agab.why: The epitope is the small part of an antigen that the antibody or receptor recognises.

mic.imm.elisa.note: ELISA: sensitive screening (HIV, hepatitis). Western blot: confirmation. PCR finds DNA directly and is the test of choice for many viruses, including monkeypox (mpox), from lesion swabs. RT-PCR for RNA viruses. Real-time PCR also measures viral load.
mic.imm.elisa.why: Mpox is confirmed by PCR on a lesion sample.

mic.app.noso.note: Hospital-acquired: appears 48 hours or more after admission. Commonest: urinary infections (catheters), then surgical site infections, pneumonia (ventilators) and line infections. Hand hygiene is the single most important prevention. MRSA, ESBL organisms, Acinetobacter and Candida auris are the problem bugs.

mic.app.bmw.note: Yellow: infectious and anatomical waste (incinerate). Red: contaminated recyclable plastics (autoclave). White puncture-proof: sharps. Blue: glass and metal implants. Do not store untreated waste over 48 hours.

mic.app.ic.note: Biosafety levels: BSL-1 harmless organisms; BSL-2 most routine pathogens; BSL-3 airborne serious ones like M. tuberculosis; BSL-4 the deadliest viruses (Ebola). Standard precautions for everyone; contact, droplet and airborne precautions by organism (N95 for TB).
mic.app.ic.why: Culturing M. tuberculosis, an airborne pathogen, needs a BSL-3 laboratory.
